sections.h1: Storefront Signs in New York City for Shops and Restaurants
sections.lead_html:
Your storefront sign is the first thing people read from the sidewalk.

Vision Graphics designs and makes storefront signs for NYC shops, restaurants, and street-level businesses, as part of our exterior signs in NYC range. We explain NYC permit rules and manage installation through licensed partners.

sections.intro_html: Exterior business signs work well as a set: a main sign above the door, an eye-level sign, and window details. Our storefront signs cover seven common options, and we can combine them in one design.

items.title: Channel Letter Signs
items.html: Individual letters mounted on the facade, lit or unlit. They read from across the street and carry your name after dark. Learn more about channel letter signs in NYC.

items.title: Dimensional Letter Signs
items.html: Raised letters or a raised logo on the sign band or wall. They give a clean, architectural look in daylight. Learn more about dimensional letter signs.

items.title: Cabinet (Lightbox) Signs
items.html: A lit box with a printed face, mounted on the facade. You can replace the face when your artwork changes, and landmark districts may limit signs lit from inside. Learn more about cabinet signs.

items.title: Blade Signs
items.html: Double-sided signs that project from the facade over the sidewalk. People walking the block see them before they see a flat sign. Learn more about blade signs.

items.title: Building Signs
items.html: Larger signs for upper walls and taller facades. They suit buildings with several tenants and signs that must read from farther away. Learn more about building signs.

items.title: Window Graphics
items.html: Vinyl lettering and graphics on the glass for hours, services, and door details. They support the main sign at eye level. Learn more about window graphics.

items.title: Panel and Metal Signs
items.html: Flat aluminum or metal panels carrying the name and logo, for wide sign bands and plain facades. They give a solid, simple look. Learn more about metal signs.

sections.after_html: Some storefronts also carry awning signs. If your building has an awning, our team can plan the new sign around it.

sections.h2: NYC Permits, Landlords and Landmark Districts
sections.intro_html: Your sign may need approvals before it goes up. The rules below are the city's, and they may change, so check them early in your plan.

items.title: DOB Sign Permit
items.html: A sign permit is generally required for a sign display or installation. A non-lit sign of about six square feet or less, or a painted sign, may need none. Zoning rules still apply.

items.title: Electrical and Illuminated Sign Permits
items.html: A lit sign needs a separate electrical permit filed by a licensed electrician. A lit sign that extends beyond the building line may also need an annual illuminated sign permit.

items.title: Zoning Size Limits
items.html: Your zoning district sets limits on sign area and lighting. In C1 and C2 districts, lit signs may total up to three times your street frontage in feet, with a 50-square-foot cap. Non-lit signs follow the same three-times rule, with a 150-square-foot cap.

items.title: Licensed Sign Hangers
items.html: A licensed sign hanger performs or supervises most sign installations and removals. Exemptions cover signs up to 75 square feet and 25 pounds, and a registered general contractor may install non-lit business signs with limited text. A licensed sign hanger must have a place of business in NYC.

items.title: Landlord Approval
items.html: Your lease may set sign rules, and your landlord or building management may need to approve the design before work starts. Send any lease sign criteria early, and we will prepare the drawings they ask for. We can provide a certificate of insurance upon request, and our team confirms your building's requirements.

items.title: Landmark Districts and LPC Review
items.html: In a landmark or historic district, LPC reviews exterior signs. Staff cannot approve exterior signs lit from inside, which includes front-lit channel letters. Halo-lit solid letters with a concealed light source may qualify if they meet the pin-mounted limits.

items.title: Local Law 15 of 2026
items.html: DOB will not issue work-without-a-permit violations for certain accessory signs, including business storefront signs, that existed on or before February 9, 2025. That runs through February 8, 2028, with temporary assistance through August 7, 2028. It does not make a noncompliant sign lawful and does not cover a new replacement sign.

sections.after_html: Permit paperwork is part of the plan our project lead manages. Ask our team who files for your sign and which approvals apply at your address.

sections.intro_html: Store signs work differently for each kind of street-level business. Match the sign set to how people find you.

items.title: Restaurant Facade Signs
items.html: Restaurant facade signs in NYC need to be spotted from the street and clear at night. Storefront restaurant signs often pair halo-lit letters, a blade sign, and window graphics. See restaurant signs in NYC.

items.title: Retail
items.html: Retail store signs compete with busy blocks and neighboring shop signs. A clear sign band, a blade sign, and window graphics help shoppers find the door. See retail store signs in NYC.

items.title: Salons and Clinics
items.html: Salons, clinics, and neighborhood services need a calm, readable sign and clear door details. Hours, services, and booking information fit well on the glass.

items.title: Street-Level Offices
items.html: Street-level offices need a sign that reads clearly as a business entrance. A sign band or panel with matching door lettering does that job. See signs for offices and properties.

sections.html:
Manhattan storefronts often sit on dense blocks with shared building rules and landmark districts. See storefront signage in Manhattan.

Brooklyn storefronts range from busy commercial corridors to quiet side streets, and the right sign often depends on the block. See storefront signage in Brooklyn.

sections.h2: How a Storefront Sign Project Works
sections.intro_html: Five steps take you from a photo to an installed sign. A Vision Graphics project lead is your single point of contact throughout.
steps:
Send Photos and Measurements

Send photos of your storefront, the sign band width, and your logo. Our team asks follow-up questions. See the sign quote checklist for NYC for what to include.

Design and Drawing

We prepare a drawing of the new sign on your storefront before anything is made. You confirm size, position, and finish, and the drawing supports landlord review.

Permits and Approvals

Our project lead manages the paperwork and building approvals with your landlord. Lit signs need a licensed electrician, and landmark blocks may need extra review.

Fabrication

We make most signs at our Salt Lake City production facility and ship them to your project. Specialty items can come from other Vision Graphics locations or trusted partners.

Installation

Licensed installation partners install your sign, and a licensed electrician connects lit signs. A Vision Graphics project lead manages the schedule, building access, and paperwork. See how sign installation in NYC works.

items.q: How much does a storefront sign cost in NYC?
items.a_html: Most storefront signs cost roughly $1,500 to $12,000 or more for the sign itself, depending on type, size, and lighting. A typical NYC channel letter set runs about $4,000 to $12,000. Installation is priced separately. Treat these as planning ranges that your quote replaces.

items.q: Do I need a permit for a storefront sign in NYC, and do you handle it?
items.a_html: Often yes. DOB generally requires a sign permit, and a non-lit sign of about six square feet or less, or a painted sign, may need none. Lit signs also need an electrical permit. Our project lead manages the paperwork, and our team confirms who files for your address.

items.q: How long does it take from approval to installation?
items.a_html: Most signs take 1 to 5 weeks to make and ship after you approve the drawing, plus time for city review. Simple graphics take 1 to 2 weeks, dimensional or metal signs 2 to 4, and lit signs 3 to 5. A full channel letter project runs about six to ten weeks.

items.q: Can you remove my old sign as part of the job?
items.a_html: Yes. Removal is part of the install plan. Wall patching and paint touch-up are included in your quote, and our team will confirm the details. Send a photo of your old sign and the surrounding facade, and we'll plan the removal with the new sign.

items.q: Do you install early morning or after hours?
items.a_html: Yes. We schedule installs around your building's rules, including early mornings, evenings, and weekends. After-hours work can add labor charges, and we confirm them in your quote. Licensed installation partners handle the installation, and our project lead manages the schedule.

We serve all five boroughs: Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx, and Staten Island. We make signs in Salt Lake City and install them through licensed partners, with one Vision Graphics project lead as your contact. Send your storefront address and photos, and our team confirms scheduling for your block.

items.q: How big can a storefront sign be in NYC?
items.a_html: Your zoning district sets the limit. In C1 and C2 districts, lit signs may total up to three times your street frontage in feet, capped at 50 square feet. Non-lit signs follow the same rule, with a 150-square-foot cap. Your lease and any landmark rules can set lower limits, and our team checks your district.

items.q: Can I light my sign in a landmark district?
items.a_html: Possibly, with limits. LPC staff cannot approve exterior signs lit from inside, which includes front-lit channel letters and cabinet signs. Halo-lit solid letters with a concealed light source may qualify if they meet the pin-mounted limits of 18 inches tall and 2 inches deep. Other proposals may go to a public hearing.

items.q: Does Local Law 15 cover my existing sign?
items.a_html: It may. Local Law 15 of 2026 pauses work-without-a-permit violations for certain accessory signs, including business storefront signs, that existed on or before February 9, 2025, through February 8, 2028. It does not make a noncompliant sign lawful and does not cover a new replacement sign. Ask our team to review yours.

items.a_html: Vision Graphics designs and makes storefront signs for NYC shops and restaurants, with a 60-year history and production in Salt Lake City. Licensed installation partners handle installation, managed by one Vision Graphics project lead. We serve all five boroughs. Send a photo of your storefront, and our team replies with questions, a drawing, and a quote.
